title: Julia DV
content: It was a very hot day in July. I was riding my bike when I decided to stop at the mall to get a bottle of water. My breathing was labored but bearable. As soon as I entered the McDonald’s, the first thing I noticed was the air conditioning was blasting. I started sweating and breathing heavily, but was still conscious. I approached the self-order screen and began pressing it, but it wasn’t working. I grew agitated but tried to stay calm. I continued to press the button, but it still didn't work. I turned my head to the left, vaguely remembering a guy in front of me. Then everything went dark. I fainted and collapsed to the ground. Before I fell, I felt my senses shutting down. There was no touch or no taste. The sounds around me disappeared. I didn’t feel myself closing my eyes or seeing complete darkness. Suddenly, I didn’t even feel the fall. When I regained consciousness, I was lying on the floor with a nurse by my side who was trying to wake me up. She told me I had been unconscious for about 30 minutes, that my lips were purple, my complexion had turned pale, I was cold, and she couldn’t detect a pulse. During the time I was unconscious, I had an experience. I found myself in a white and gray hallway. I was positioned on the right side. To my left side was another hallway, with a line of motionless people in the middle as the line turned right. They were women, men, and young people. I stood still and watched them. One guy turned to look straight into my eyes. He gave me a vacant look, like he was mentally not there. I remember thinking, "I don’t understand why I’m here." I’m not religious, and I never have been. Yet, the main feeling was that I was in purgatory, waiting in line without knowing why. It was like I had something unresolved to do or say. There were no emotions. The people in line seemed resigned; some with their heads down. Something has changed in my life since then. I’ve developed the ability to distinguish dreams from memories, and I can say with certainty that this wasn’t a dream. It was too vivid and too strange. My experience was filled with silent resignation and regret. And the people there looked at me with a sense of pity.

elements.At the time of your experience, was ther: No, Direct head injury, Life threatening event, but not clinical death
elements.Did you feel separated from your body?: I lost awareness of my body
elements.How did your highest level of consciousn: Less consciousness and alertness than normal, I felt nothing, as if I was resigned or didn't understand what was happening, because at that moment, the corridor was reality.
elements.At what time during the experience were: I fainted for 30 minutes or more. I remember that in that corridor, about 20 minutes of time had passed.
elements.Did time seem to speed up or slow down?: Time seemed to go faster or slower than usual, Time was real; they were there for 20 minutes.
elements.Please compare your vision during the ex: Everything turned black, then I found myself in a corridor.
elements.Please compare your hearing during the e: All sounds stopped; there were no sounds or breaths.
elements.Did you encounter or become aware of any: Yes, There was no relation to the people I had never seen before. But I knew they were souls, not bodies.
elements.Did you seem to enter some other, uneart: Some unfamiliar and strange place, It was strange because it was bright but there were no lights. Some walls were darker and others lighter, but I was calm and knew I was safe.
elements.What emotions did you feel during the ex: Resignation, confusion. All my emotions or feelings were extinguished, they no longer existed. Emptiness. Apathy.
elements.Did you feel a sense of harmony or unity: I felt united or one with the world
elements.Did your experience include features con: Content that was entirely not consistent with the beliefs you had at the time of your experience
elements.During your experience, did you gain inf: Yes, I realized that there actually is something because I was there.
elements.What life changes occurred in your life: I became more apathetic, indifferent, logical, and inclined to not solve problems.
elements.How accurately do you remember the exper: I remember the experience more accurately than other life events that occurred around the time of the experience
elements.Do you have any psychic, non-ordinary or: Yes, My intuition, the ability to distinguish dreams from memories.
elements.Are there one or several parts of your e: That I didn't see anyone I knew.
elements.What did you believe about the reality o: Experience was definitely real, Because I began to understand and distinguish a dream from reality. The dreams were more vague, random, and constantly moving; this was always the same. The people moved normally, nothing was weird. I was there standing, observing, perceiving, carefully looking at the details of where I was.
elements.What do you believe about the reality of: Experience was definitely real, I remain faithful to what I thought; nothing has changed
